documentation:
## View image

### What it does

This compound will read a texture in from disk and display a diagnostic.  A texture is made of one or more images, in a texture-atlas (such as "UDIM") space.

### Inputs and outputs

The image to read is one that is included with the default Maya installation. It can be set to any image. The output is a Bifrost Object.

### How it works

- The `read_texture` node is used to read a texture from a file.

- The `file_path` input recognises some tokens for path resolution as well as supporting environment variables and frame numbers in the filename.  Please see the compound info tab for more details.

- The compound supports `file_color_space` input as a string.  If left as the default empty string the node will attempt to determine the colorspace automatically using OpenColorIO.  Use "raw" to bypass any colorspace conversion.

_notes.text:
This example graph uses an image that is included with the Bifrost installation. 

Disconnect ***expand_env_vars*** then change the *file_path* on the ***read_texture*** compound to a path to the desired image on disk.

# read_texture

This compound will read a texture in from disk and display a diagnostic.

The compound reads a texture into a Bifrost *object* that can then be passed along to be used in other graphs.

# texture_scope
While there is also a ***texture_scope*** inside ***read_texture*** to display the image in the viewport, the scope provided here is also adding an emissive texture for rendering. 

Please see compound the info tabs for more information.

A **texture** is different from an **image**.
A **texture** is made of one or more images, in a texture-atlas (such as "UDIM") space.

The ***read_texture*** compound supports image sequences through the *frame* port as well as color space through the *color_space port*.
